description: A hurdy-gurdy drone instrument: one rosined wheel bows six strings at once, so every revolution lays the same ripple of level and brightness over all of them

params.text: Sets the root of the key, which moves all six voices together
Picks the scale the voice degrees are read from; it takes the whole scale another module sends, including a non-octave or Scala one
Sets how fast the wheel turns, in revolutions per second, which is the tempo of everything the module does
Sets how many strokes the turn is divided into, one to eight
Sets how hard the wheel bears on the strings overall; it changes the timbre before it changes the level, the way bow pressure does
Sets how deeply the wheel's irregularity reaches the sound: it is a fixed profile of eccentricity, uneven rosin and a dip at the seam, in the same place every turn
Raises the threshold a stroke has to clear before the loose bridge foot buzzes, so turning it up thins the pattern from every stroke to the accented ones to the downbeat alone
Snaps every voice to the nearest whole-number ratio against the root rather than to equal temperament
Sets how long the buzz takes to die away
Sets which octave the root voice sounds in
Sets which degree of the scale that voice sounds, so the voicing stays in key whatever the key is
Sets which octave that voice sounds in
Morphs that voice's wave through sine, triangle, sawtooth and square; the sawtooth is what a bowed string really does, and moving toward square reads as more bow pressure
Sets that voice's phase against the others, which holds steady only once the temper control has snapped the tuning to whole-number ratios
Sets how hard that one string bears on the wheel; a string barely touching it is duller, slips, and gives more rosin noise than tone
Puts that string on the wheel, and is what its gate jack replaces when one is patched; either way the string swells onto the wheel rather than switching on

inputs.text: Sets the root, a volt per octave, added to the root knob
Picks the scale, one volt per scale, added to the scale knob
Changes the wheel speed, added to the crank knob
Changes how many strokes the turn is divided into, added to the coups knob
Changes the overall wheel pressure, added to the pressure knob
Changes how deeply the wheel's irregularity is heard, added to the ripple knob
Changes the buzz threshold, added to the dog knob
Changes how far the tuning is snapped to whole-number ratios, added to the temper knob
A rise fires a stroke at the hardest strength there is, so it buzzes whatever the dog knob is set to
One rise locks one revolution of the wheel, so the whole instrument runs in time with the patch
A high gate puts that string on the wheel, taking its button's place
Morphs that voice's wave, added to its wave knob
Changes that voice's phase against the others, added to its phase knob
Changes how long the buzz takes to die away, added to the decay knob
Changes how hard that string bears on the wheel, added to its pressure knob
Moves the root voice, one volt per octave, added to its octave fader
Moves that voice, one volt per scale degree, added to its degree fader
Changes that voice's level, added to its level fader

outputs.text: The left side of the six voices
The right side of the six voices
The six voices on six polyphonic channels, the sixth being the buzzing string
The wheel's own irregularity as a control voltage, which is the same ripple the six voices are hearing
A trigger every time the loose bridge foot actually buzzes

notes: the module drones as soon as it is placed: the wheel turns at the crank setting whether or not anything is patched
the strip along the foot of the display is the turn unwrapped, one bar per stroke, and clicking a bar silences that stroke; the display cannot be reached by clicking for help
a stroke does more than buzz: it lifts the wheel's speed for a moment, so all the drones swell and brighten with it, which is half of why an accent lands
the temper control does almost nothing on a voicing of roots, octaves and fifths, because equal temperament is already within two cents there; it bites on thirds, sixths and sevenths
menu: Gate presses the string — makes a voice's gate press the string onto the wheel rather than acting as a plain amplifier on it
Gate press time — a slider setting how long a gated string takes to swell onto the wheel
Wheel — a label over the five wheel sliders below it
Wheel spread — a slider setting how far apart the six voices are placed around the wheel
Detune — a slider setting how far the six voices are detuned from one another
Rosin — a slider setting how much rosin noise the wheel gives
Body — a slider setting how much of the instrument's body resonance is heard
Stereo width — a slider setting how far the six voices are spread across the stereo image
All strings on the wheel — puts every string on the wheel at once
Every stroke of the turn — restores every stroke of the turn, undoing any that were silenced on the display
